title: Try follow Spark QuickStart on Docker spark:python3 container
question:
I try to follow Spark QuickStart on quick-start in the Spark documentation. I'm having trouble since I'm using a Docker container (spark: python 3). The main issue is that instructions order to find a file README.md but the docker is initiated on /opt/spark/bin/pyspark.

What kind of docker order should I give to docker to load the container and let me follow instructions on Spark QuickStart? For example

textFile = spark.read.text("README.md")
answer:
If I understand the setup correctly you launched a single container with distribution of spark inside of it.
The command is something like this:



docker run -it spark:python3 /opt/spark/bin/pyspark

The easiest way to read some file from host is to read it from volume
Put a desired file for reading somewhere on your hostsystem and mount it inside the docker container

docker run -it  -v /somewhereOnHost/pom.xml:/tmp/pom.xml spark:python3 /opt/spark/bin/pyspark

And the code works


SparkSession available as 'spark'.
>>> tx = spark.read.text("/tmp/pom.xml")
>>> tx.count()
196
>>>

But, anyway, my recommendation is not to focus on containers when you start getting familiar with spark, because it gives you additional layer of complexity (especially if you start using k8s)

I'd recommend the following setup for quick start and further deep dive:

  1. Install java 17/21 (with PATH and JAVA_HOME variables because spark will need it)
  2. Download spark binaries from https://spark.apache.org/downloads.html
  3. Extract it somewhere and set in env (example)

export SPARK_HOME=/usr/local/spark-3.5.4/spark-3.5.4-bin-hadoop3-scala2.13
export PATH=$PATH:$SPARK_HOME/bin
  1. Run pyspark in your terminal and enjoy

I might missed something (perhaps python3 has to be installed because you're using pyspark) but it will be easy to figure out.
With such a setup you ll be able to run and try local/client/cluster modes with spark, not just a local shell.
